g.text: CGNAT: the ISP puts YOU behind its NAT too
Two NATs in a row. You control the first one. The second belongs to the ISP.
Port forwarding on YOUR router (NAT #1) is useless: the packet is dropped at the ISP's NAT (#2) before it reaches you.
So friends behind CGNAT must connect OUTWARD: to a relay, or to each other at the same moment (hole punching).
Spot it: hops in your traceroute (and your router's WAN address) inside 100.64.0.0/10. Tailscale ALSO uses 100.64.0.0/10 for its own addresses;
by default its Linux client drops incoming CGNAT-range packets that are not from Tailscale, so the two do not collide.
